reading_head: Seventy-One Hours, and Nothing Wrong on Board
reading_sub: A commercial delay caused entirely by two documents

paras: A container vessel of 41,000 gross tonnage arrived at the outer anchorage on a Friday evening and was cleared to berth the following morning. Discharge began at 0700. By midday the port authority had stopped the operation and placed forty-one containers under seal.

The reason was documentary rather than physical. The bill of lading described the consignment as machinery parts in transit, consigned to a buyer in a third country and not intended for entry. The stowage plan, however, showed the same containers in a hold that had been declared empty on arrival, and the freight had been prepaid to this port and no further. Nothing on board had been tampered with. The papers simply described two different voyages.

The operator had the containers surveyed the same afternoon and had the discrepancy traced to the loading port, where a clerk had amended the stowage plan by hand after the bill of lading had been issued. The agent then got the documents reissued and had the amended set lodged with the port authority before the end of the following working day.

Clearance was restored on the Tuesday. The vessel had lost seventy-one hours, and the charterer had the delay costed at just under forty thousand dollars. The port authority found that no offence had been committed, but recommended that operators have the two documents reconciled before arrival rather than after seal. It is a recommendation the industry has heard before and has not yet had implemented.

grammar_question: In all four sentences the subject did not do the work. Say who did, in each case -- and then find the one thing the four sentences have in common, in the same position every time.
grammar_rows: the subject arranges it; somebody else performs it
the same idea, less formal, often with effort or pressure behind it
the noun sits BETWEEN the two verbs. That is what separates the causative from a perfect tense
should, must, will + have + object + participle

had the delay costed is NOT the past perfect of cost. If there is a noun between had and the participle, the subject did not do the work -- and an option that says the charterer calculated the figure himself is adding a fact the text does not carry.
grammar_insight: The causative is how commercial English says who is responsible without saying who is at the keyboard. In the options the swap is always the same: the arranger is turned into the performer, and everything else is left untouched.

prod_sub: Two recordings, then the case in your own words

listenings.sub: The man who had the documents reissued explains his Saturday. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: I got the call at half past twelve. Forty-one boxes under seal, discharge stopped, and a master who wanted to know whether he was going to be arrested. He was not. Nothing on board was wrong. What was wrong was on paper. I had the containers surveyed that same afternoon, because until somebody physically opens one, everything you say to the authority is an opinion. Then I had the discrepancy traced back to the loading port, and it took about two hours to find it: a clerk had amended the stowage plan by hand after the bill of lading was already issued. Nobody was hiding anything. Somebody was tidying up. I got the whole set reissued overnight and had it lodged first thing on the Monday. Clearance came back on the Tuesday. Seventy-one hours, and not one of them was about the cargo.
questions: What was the first thing he arranged, and why?
He had the containers surveyed that same afternoon, because until somebody physically opens one, everything you tell the authority is only an opinion.
What did the trace to the loading port reveal?
A clerk had amended the stowage plan by hand after the bill of lading had already been issued. Nobody was hiding anything: somebody was tidying up.
What did he do with the documents, and when was clearance restored?
He got the whole set reissued overnight and had it lodged first thing on the Monday. Clearance came back on the Tuesday.

listenings.h: What the Port Authority Looks At
listenings.sub: An inspector describes the check that stopped this ship. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: People imagine that we spend the day opening boxes. We do not. Most of what we do is comparison. We take the bill of lading, the manifest and the stowage plan, and we read them against each other, and if the three of them tell the same story the ship goes on working. When they do not, the operation stops until somebody explains why. In this case the bill said machinery parts in transit and the stowage plan put those same containers in a hold that had been declared empty on arrival. That is not a small clerical difference. On paper the cargo had two destinations and one of them was ours. We sealed the boxes rather than opening them, precisely because the problem was documentary. And I will say the thing every inspector says: have your papers reconciled before you arrive. Nobody has ever been detained for a document that agreed with itself.
questions: What does the inspector say most of the work actually is?
Comparison. They read the bill of lading, the manifest and the stowage plan against each other, and the ship keeps working only if the three tell the same story.
What was the specific difference in this case?
The bill said machinery parts in transit, and the stowage plan put those same containers in a hold that had been declared empty on arrival. On paper the cargo had two destinations.
Why were the containers sealed rather than opened?
Precisely because the problem was documentary and not physical.

quiz.q: The operator had the containers surveyed. Who opened the containers?
opts: The operator, personally.
A surveyor. The operator arranged it; somebody else did the work.
The port authority, on the operator's behalf.

quiz.q: What separates had the delay costed from the past perfect had costed?
opts: Nothing. They are two ways of writing the same thing.
The noun between the two verbs. With it, the subject did not perform the action.
The tense. One is past and the other is present.

quiz.q: The industry has not yet had the recommendation implemented. What does the sentence say?
opts: That the industry rejected the recommendation.
That the industry has not arranged for anybody to put it into practice.
That the industry implemented it and then withdrew it.

grammar_tip_title: The Causative -- Have and Get Something Done
grammar_tip_lead: Commercial English needs a way of saying who is responsible without saying who is at the keyboard. That is the causative, and the giveaway is always the same: a noun sitting between the two verbs.

teacher.s1: Abertura (2 min): DECISAO DE DESENHO, valida para o programa inteiro: toda aula e reading-driven, sem alternar com aula de fala (a REGRA 29.2 nao se aplica aqui), porque a prova e 100% leitura. Entre direto, sem cumprimento scriptado (REGRA 27A).
teacher.s2: Homework check + warm-up (5 min): Ela leu um bill of lading real. Peca os tres campos que ela reconheceu e a linha que ela nao decodificou. O que voce mede: ela procura por CAMPO ou le o documento como texto corrido? Documento tecnico se le por campo, e isso vale ponto na prova.
teacher.s3: Provocacao (5 min): A frase e a aula inteira. Pergunte: who opened the containers? Se ela responder 'the operator', otimo -- e o erro que este slide existe para produzir. Nao corrija ainda; deixe a descoberta para o capitulo 4.
teacher.s4: Objetivo (2 min): Diga: the words of the trade, the structure that hides the worker, and the same swap as always.
teacher.s5: Transicao vocab (1 min): Diga: Ten words that decide money, not safety. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s6: Vocab reveal 1-4 (5 min): freight, consignment, bill of lading, port authority. NAO traduza (REGRA 13). CCQ para freight: Is freight the goods or the money? (Both -- e a ambiguidade e usada em prova.) CCQ para bill of lading: Is it a receipt or a contract? (As duas coisas, e tambem titulo de propriedade.)
teacher.s7: Vocab reveal 5-7 (5 min): clearance, stowage, hold. CCQ para clearance: Is clearance the same as the under-keel clearance from Lesson 1? (Nao -- mesma palavra, outro sentido: aqui e permissao oficial. E o mesmo mecanismo do 'port' da aula 2.) Aponte isso: e a terceira vez que a prova pode usar palavra conhecida em sentido desconhecido.
teacher.s8: Vocab reveal 8-10 (5 min): gross tonnage, discharge, in transit. CCQ para gross tonnage: Is a ship of 41,000 gross tonnage 41,000 tonnes heavy? (NAO -- e volume fechado, nao peso. Erro classico e ja caiu.) CCQ para discharge: Does discharge here mean firing a weapon or releasing a patient? (Nenhum dos dois: e descarregar carga. Falso amigo de contexto.)
teacher.s9: Consolidate (4 min): Ela toca a palavra e le a definicao em voz alta antes de fechar o par.
teacher.s10: Transicao leitura (1 min): Diga: Nothing on this ship was wrong. It still lost three days. O proximo slide e o de TAREFA: a pergunta ANTES do texto.
teacher.s11: Leitura (7 min): Tres minutos em silencio, sem dicionario. NAO traduza. Depois UMA frase de resumo.
teacher.s12: Gist (3 min): Ela escolhe e JUSTIFICA. A opcao (a) e a armadilha: o cenario sugere contrabando e o texto diz explicitamente que nao houve infracao.
teacher.s13: True or False (7 min): REGRA DA CASA: TRUE ou FALSE e DEPOIS a linha que prova. A afirmacao 2 e conversao (71 horas = pouco menos de 3 dias) e a 5 inverte 'to this port and no further'.
teacher.s14: Transicao gramatica (1 min): Diga: Now we answer the question from slide 3. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s15: Grammar discovery (7 min): Nao de a regra. Pergunte, para cada exemplo: who did the work? Depois: what is in the same position in all four sentences? Espere ela achar o OBJETO no meio. So entao clique Reveal the Rule. CCQ decisivo: 'The charterer had the delay costed' -- did the charterer do the maths? (Nao.) Ela estuda gramatica sozinha: aqui e ferramenta de leitura.
teacher.s16: Practice (4 min): Ela diz a forma ORALMENTE antes de clicar.
teacher.s17: Spot the error (4 min): Os quatro sao de ORDEM: o objeto tem de ficar entre o have/get e o participio. Se ela nao vir, cubra o participio com o dedo e pergunte o que falta no meio.
teacher.s18: Transicao equivalencia (1 min): Diga: Same three days, in the words the trade uses. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s19: Como a prova esconde (4 min): Os quatro pares saiam do texto. Pergunte, para cada um: which of the two is on the page?
teacher.s20: Equivalencia (5 min): Depois de fechar os pares, cubra a direita e faca a direcao dificil.
teacher.s21: Complete (5 min): Teacher-led, uma lacuna por vez. As oito respostas sao oito das dez palavras da aula.
teacher.s22: Quick fire (6 min): Uma por vez, em voz alta, antes das dicas. A terceira (had costed x had the delay costed) e a que vale ponto.
teacher.s23: Transicao (1 min): Diga: The agent who fixed it, and the inspector who stopped it. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s24: Listening 1 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Escuta medida em 0%: comece em 0.75x. Toque duas vezes, sem texto. Conte com ela quantos causativos o agente usa (sao cinco).
teacher.s25: Listening 2 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Esta e a visao do OUTRO lado, e e a frase final que interessa: have your papers reconciled before you arrive. Pergunte se ela percebeu o causativo dentro do conselho.
teacher.s26: Role-play guiado (4 min): Cinco frases com os frames. Conte os causativos corretos e diga o numero no fim.
teacher.s27: Role-play semi-livre (5 min): O ponto e ela DIZER EM VOZ ALTA quando o texto nao informa quem executou. Aceitar 'the text does not say' e o objetivo, nao uma falha.
teacher.s28: Producao livre (6 min): Nao interrompa. Mede-se: tres causativos e a distincao documentary x physical, nomeada.
teacher.s29: Transicao wrap-up (1 min): Diga: Let us see what you can do now.
teacher.s30: Survival card (3 min): Cinco frases do proprio texto. Insista em 'bill of lading' (LAY-ding) e 'stowage' (STOH-idj) -- as duas sao pronunciadas errado por quase todo brasileiro.
teacher.s31: Checklist (2 min): Leia cada item em voz alta. Os 5 checks fecham a aula e acendem o stamp.
teacher.s32: Encerramento (2 min): Diga: Lesson 4 complete, Helena.
